name: Homestake chlorine detector
notes: Coordinate caveat: the site referenced (site:surf-surface-campus) is a surface campus point, not the detector's true ~1478 m underground location; see placement note.

placements.note: site:surf-surface-campus is an approximate campus-level point for the whole SURF/Homestake site, used because no distinct sourced coordinate exists for the Davis chlorine-tank chamber. The detector was actually ~1478 m (4850 ft) underground, not at the surface; the placement's role and dates are sourced, but the site point only marks the general campus location, not the true underground depth.
placements.quote: The experiment took place in the Homestake Gold Mine in Lead, South Dakota. ... The experiment operated continuously from 1970 until 1994.

target_mass.note: Wikipedia gives the target volume (380 m³ / 100,000 gallons of perchloroethylene) but no source consulted (checked 2026-09-18) converts this to a mass; the mass is left unset rather than computed from an assumed density.

summary.plain: A tank of dry-cleaning fluid, nearly a mile underground, that turned rare chlorine atoms into argon whenever a solar neutrino struck.
summary.technical: Radiochemical chlorine-argon detector, 380 m³ perchloroethylene target, 1478 m (4850 ft) underground in the Homestake mine; ran 1970-1994, measured 37Ar production rate 2.56±0.16(stat)±0.16(syst) SNU.

technology.note: Reaction νe + 37Cl → 37Ar + e⁻ (inverse beta decay) and the extraction/counting steps: Cleveland et al. 1998 abstract (src:homestake-1998-flux-measurement). Perchloroethylene tank, argon extraction by helium sweep every two to three months: Davis Nobel lecture (quoted). The 'dry-cleaning fluid' gloss is from Wikipedia.
technology.quote: build a 100,000-gallon chlorine-argon neutrino detector in the Homestake Gold Mine ... In order to extract argon from the tank, helium is bubbled through the perchloroethylene.
technology.value: Radiochemical chlorine detector: solar neutrinos capture on 37Cl to produce 37Ar via inverse beta decay in a large tank of perchloroethylene (dry-cleaning fluid), with the argon periodically extracted and counted
